front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《49》

en: A moment of daze, not knowing
That autumn day before my eyes
Leaving behind, the chinaberry tree in the wind
Beneath the pine, no boy in sight
The clouds run deep, the hermit nowhere to be seen
The green mountains remain, the setting sun still red

points.zh:
松下問童子，言師採藥去。
只在此山中，雲深不知處。
--唐。賈島 《尋隱者不遇》
滾滾長江東逝水，浪花淘盡英雄。
是非成敗轉頭空，青山依舊在，幾度夕陽紅。
白髮漁樵江渚上，慣看秋月春風。
一壺濁酒喜相逢，古今多少事，都付笑談中
--清。楊慎《臨江仙》
points.en:
Beneath the pines I asked the boy;
he said, his master had gone to gather herbs.
He is only somewhere on this mountain,
but the clouds are deep, and I know not where.
-- Tang dynasty. Jia Dao, 'Seeking the Hermit but Not Finding Him'
The rolling waters of the Yangtze flow ever eastward, its waves washing away all heroes.
Right and wrong, success and failure, all turn to nothing in a single glance back; the green mountains remain as before, through however many crimson sunsets.
White-haired fishermen and woodcutters on the river's sandbanks, long used to the autumn moon and spring breeze.
A jug of turbid wine, a joyful meeting; the affairs of past and present, all given over to laughter and talk.
-- Ming dynasty. Yang Shen, 'Linjiangxian'

en: Old temple, a pond
The frog, leaping into
Splash the banana haiku

points.zh:
日本俳句詩人松尾芭蕉的經典俳句:
古寺池塘
青蛙，跳入
水聲響
points.en:
A classic haiku by the Japanese haiku poet Matsuo Basho:
An old temple pond—
a frog leaps in,
the sound of water.

en: The wind says
Take your sorrow
Give it back to the sparse, faint color of grass

zh: 隨愛麗絲夢遊仙境，陶醉
en: Walking into Burger King, I am king
Order a bit of Daily Queen, you are the queen
Following Alice into Wonderland, intoxicated

points.zh:
《 愛麗絲夢遊仙境 》名言 ：
「凡事都有寓意，只要你肯去找。」
「在我的領地中，妳要一直拚命跑，才能保持在同一個位置；如果你想前進，就必須跑得      比現在快兩倍才行。」
「如果你不知道你要去哪裡， 那麼現在你在哪裡，一點都不重要。」
「不能總是為了別人而活，決定權在你自己，因為當你面對那些怪獸，你就得獨自戰鬥！」
「我已經受夠了你們對我身份的指責，這是我的夢境。從現在起一切由我說了算，我會開出一條路。」
points.en:
Famous quotations from "Alice in Wonderland":
"Everything has a moral, if only you can find it."
"In my domain, you have to run as fast as you can just to stay in the same place; if you want to get somewhere else, you must run at least twice as fast as that."
"If you don't know where you are going, then it doesn't matter at all where you are now."
"You cannot always live for others; the decision is yours alone, because when you face those monsters, you must fight them by yourself."
"I have had enough of you all questioning who I am -- this is my dream. From now on, I decide everything, and I will find my own way forward."

en: Turning back suddenly, that person
Yet there, where the lights grow dim
And then what?

points.zh:
眾里尋他千百度，驀然回首，那人卻在，燈火闌珊處。
--宋。辛棄疾《青玉案》
points.en:
Among the crowds I searched for her a thousand times, ten thousand times; then, suddenly turning my head, there she was, in the dim light where the lanterns wane.
-- Song dynasty. Xin Qiji, 'Green Jade Cup'

en: Is it a dancer's pose? Is it Zen contemplation?
Following Tong Yang-Tze, walking into
Words of aesthetics, their ink-rhythm like the wind

points.zh: 董陽孜（1942年10月6日－）台灣書法藝術家。1942年出生上海、十歲來台，大學就讀國立臺灣師範大學美術學系，求學期間曾先後向張穀年、丁念先、臺靜農、張隆延與傅申等書畫家請益。畢業後赴美國深造藝術創作，就讀麻州大學藝術系（1966-1968），主修油畫、副修陶藝。1970年畢業後於紐約從事平面設計工作，旅美期間曾獲全美創作設計展封面設計獎。1977年返台定居後投入書藝創作。早期偏重顏真卿楷書和魏碑創作，近年偏向王羲之和懷素的書法感覺，創作中溶入西洋構圖理論，兼具現代平面設計與傳統書法的美學。自2002年至2018年前後約十五年間，董陽孜在既成創作風格上，探索大尺幅創作。大開大闔的巨幅書寫，挑戰觀眾對書法作品的觀展體驗。「巨大書寫對於藝術家的創作與觀眾觀賞均產生與傳統書法截然不同的挑戰。藝術家的書寫由書案式創作轉為環境裡的空間運動，作品的大面積對觀眾形成環境式觀賞，改變了傳統上作品與觀眾的關係。」身為台灣重要書藝家，董陽孜即使已過古稀之年，但面對創作依然不懈不怠，進來不僅跨界創作，與現代音樂，舞蹈結合，更期望將文字線條與書法表現之美，藉由不同書寫手法的詮釋，向新世代傳遞東方文字美學。
points.en: Tong Yang-Tze (born October 6, 1942) is a Taiwanese calligraphy artist. Born in Shanghai in 1942, she came to Taiwan at age ten and studied in the Fine Arts Department of National Taiwan Normal University, where during her studies she sought guidance from painters and calligraphers including Zhang Guyan, Ding Nianxian, Tai Jingnong, Zhang Longyan, and Fu Shen. After graduating she went to the United States to further her artistic training, studying in the Art Department of the University of Massachusetts (1966–1968), majoring in oil painting with a minor in ceramics. After graduating in 1970 she worked in graphic design in New York, and during her years in the U.S. won a national creative design competition's cover design award. After returning to settle in Taiwan in 1977, she devoted herself to calligraphic creation. In her early period she favored the regular script of Yan Zhenqing and the style of Northern Wei steles; in recent years she has leaned toward the calligraphic sensibility of Wang Xizhi and Huaisu, incorporating Western compositional theory into her work, blending the aesthetics of modern graphic design with traditional calligraphy. From roughly 2002 to 2018, some fifteen years, Tong Yang-Tze, building on her established style, explored large-scale works. Her sweeping, monumental calligraphy challenges the audience's experience of viewing calligraphic art. "Monumental writing poses a challenge, quite different from traditional calligraphy, for both the artist's creative process and the audience's viewing experience. The artist's writing shifts from being created at a desk to being a spatial movement within an environment; the large scale of the work creates an environmental, immersive viewing experience for the audience, transforming the traditional relationship between work and viewer." As one of Taiwan's leading calligraphy artists, Tong Yang-Tze, even past the age of seventy, remains tireless in her creative work. In recent years she has not only worked across disciplines, collaborating with contemporary music and dance, but hopes, through the interpretation of different modes of writing, to pass the beauty of textual line and calligraphic expression on to a new generation, conveying the aesthetics of East Asian script.

en: Dusk fades into the distant mountains
Willow branches reflected in the pond
The hours spent grinding ink
The journey is long, how many days
The evening wind brushes the willows, and my mood falls into
Li Shutong's mountains beyond mountains

points.zh:
《 送別 》
詞/編曲：李叔同   原曲：John P. Ordway
長亭外，古道邊，芳草碧連天
晚風拂柳笛聲殘，夕陽山外山
天之涯，地之角，知交半零落
一瓢濁酒盡餘歡，今宵別夢寒
points.en:
"Farewell"
Lyrics/Arrangement: Li Shutong; Original melody: John P. Ordway
Outside the roadside pavilion, along the old road, fragrant grass stretches green to the horizon
the evening wind stirs the willows, the flute's sound fades away, the setting sun beyond the mountains, and mountains beyond that
At the edge of the sky, at the corner of the earth, old friends are scattered, half of them gone
one gourd of cloudy wine to finish what joy remains, tonight, in the dream of parting, all is cold
